children: The Consumer Price Index report for August indicated a 3.4% year-over-year increase to match the consensus expectation.

Beef prices moderated slightly during August, with uncooked beef roasts down 1.7% month over month and beef steaks 1.5% lower, although both categories showed prices much higher than a year ago. Uncooked ground beef prices were up 7.2% from a year ago but flat on a sequential basis.

Beef prices rose to record levels earlier in the year due to a combination of supply shortages driven by long-term droughts, high feed costs, reduced cattle inventories, and strong consumer demand for beef. Notably, the national cattle herd is at its lowest level in decades. Severe droughts over the last five years have forced ranchers to reduce breeding herds as grazing lands and feed became scarce. The replenishment cycle is expected to take several years.

President Trump temporarily reduced barriers to importing up to 300K metric tons of lean beef trimmings, mainly used in ground beef, to attempt to increase supply and put downward pressure on prices. He also signed measures meant to expand meat processing and support cattle producers, but the near-term effect on supermarket prices is expected to be limited in the near term.
A broad list of companies impacted by beef prices includes JBS N.V.

title: CPI read: Beef prices tick lower in August, still notably higher than a year ago
